key_insight: VISOR reduces LVLM inference cost by performing sparse, dynamically selected vision–language interactions “on request” instead of compressing or discarding visual tokens, preserving fine-grained information while cutting compute.
problem_solved: Existing efficiency methods compress visual tokens, creating an information bottleneck that degrades performance on fine-grained understanding and reasoning tasks; VISOR addresses this by keeping visual information intact and only activating cross-modal computation when needed.
method: Keep rich visual feature maps intact, but avoid always-on cross-modal processing.
Use a lightweight, dynamic selector/gating mechanism that triggers vision–language interactions only for relevant queries or tokens (“on request”).
Cache or skip unnecessary cross-attention steps to realize sparse conditional computation and lower inference FLOPs without sacrificing accuracy.
impact: Maintains high accuracy on detailed multimodal tasks while substantially lowering latency and compute cost, making large vision–language models more practical and cost-effective to deploy.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: full visual encoder + dynamic selector + selective cross-attention vs traditional token-reduction pipeline.
Bar/chart: compute (FLOPs or latency) vs accuracy comparing VISOR to visual-token-reduction baselines.
Sequence diagram: example query flow showing when visual interactions are triggered or skipped (“on request” gating).
Icon set: eye (vision) preserved, lightning bolt (efficiency), gate (dynamic selection), and puzzle piece (fine-grained reasoning).
paper_title: VISion On Request: Enhanced VLLM efficiency with sparse, dynamically selected, vision-language interactions
paper_authors: Adrian Bulat, Alberto Baldrati, Ioannis Maniadis Metaxas, Yassine Ouali, Georgios Tzimiropoulos
